clue.text: Strip tease imitation ?

definitions.meaning: to strip is to remove one's clothes
a mocking impersonation that teases its subject is a send-up

explanation.surface: A striptease act that merely copies someone else's.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the phrase means undress; as a noun it is a satirical impression of someone.

clue.text: Worked on the books, also took first place

parts.note: too means also
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: Someone who did the accounts and also came top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked on the books' is not bookkeeping: bookbinders decorate leather covers with heated tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooled leather bindings are stamped with decorative designs using hot hand tools.

clue.text: Cape Kennedy's opening can provide joint cover

indicators.note: the letters can be made to provide the answer by rearranging them, signalled loosely here

parts.note: the opening three letters of the name Kennedy

explanation.surface: The opening of the Florida launch site at Cape Kennedy offering protection to a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: The page reads 'Cape', not 'Caps'. 'can provide' asks for an anagram of CAPE plus KEN, the start of Kennedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the small bone covering the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: Astronomical number the Italian brightened the company up with

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' tells you to read the run of pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: il is the Italian for 'the'
lit means brightened
co is the abbreviation for company
on can mean with, as in cheese on toast

explanation.surface: An Italian man cheering up his firm with a huge figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ILLITCO into OCTILLI; then ON follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge number, ten to the 27th power in modern usage, the sort of figure astronomers deal in.

clue.text: Game birds obstruct the hunter

definitions.meaning: a board game for two players
in this game several pieces representing waterfowl try to hem in a single predator piece

explanation.surface: Game birds getting in a hunter's way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game birds' reads as one phrase, but 'Game' is a definition on its own: in this board game the many geese try to trap the single fox.
explanation.definitionFit: An old board game in which a fox and a flock of geese are the pieces, the geese trying to pen the fox in.

clue.text: It's real in the form of a cross

indicators.note: the letters of the first words are recast into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insisting a thing is genuine, shaped like a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the form of' tells you to rearrange ITSREAL, the letters of 'It's real'.
explanation.definitionFit: The St Andrew's flag shows a diagonal X-shaped cross, the heraldic name for which is this word.

clue.text: For some sob-sisters, a description?

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the words that follow are used, so the answer is hidden in them

explanation.surface: Asking how one might describe some sentimental women journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: A sob-sister is a journalist who writes tearjerking stories. The answer runs across 'sisterS A Description'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearjerking writers deal in sorrow, so an adjective meaning unhappy describes their work.

clue.text: Singers on the way up

parts.note: songbirds famous for singing as they climb high into the sky, not performers rising in the charts

explanation.surface: Up-and-coming vocalists starting to make a name for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' suggests rising stars; these singers are birds that sing as they climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylarks are songbirds that pour out song while rising steeply in flight.

clue.text: Prepare to send the economic balloon up ?

definitions.text: Prepare to send the economic balloon up

parts.words: Prepare to send the economic balloon up
parts.note: a balloon is filled with air before it is sent up, and governments that raise prices push the economy's balloon

explanation.surface: Getting ready to launch a balloon cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'economic' hints at money: price rises are called by the same name as filling a balloon with air.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow air into a balloon, and in economics to push prices and money supply up.

clue.text: Lear's daughter had one on a string

definitions.text: Lear's daughter had one on a string

parts.words: Lear's daughter had one on a string
parts.note: the name Cordelia, King Lear's youngest daughter, has strung inside it ELIA, the pen name of the writer Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: King Lear's daughter keeping someone dangling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a string' suggests a suitor kept dangling; here it means within a string of letters, as cordELIA holds Elia, Charles Lamb's pen name for his short prose pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb, writing as Elia, was famed for short reflective prose pieces.

clue.text: Apparent cut-down (so expect a refund)

parts.note: something apparent is open and plain to see
to be axed is to be cut down, as a tree is

explanation.surface: Something visibly trimmed back, with a note that money will come back to you.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed phrase is the definition: someone charged too much tax gets a rebate.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxpayer who has paid more than was due can expect money back from the revenue.

clue.text: Birds as a guide to the horses

definitions.meaning: wading birds whose males grow a frill of feathers
a racing annual named after its compiler, the standard British reference book on horses and their form

explanation.surface: Birds being used to pick winners at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruff's Guide to the Turf was a long-running British racing annual, listing horses and their form.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural names the frilled sandpipers, and the possessive names the racing reference book.

clue.text: What Silvia would do in Rome at forty, say ?

indicators.note: say signals that the Roman letters are to be spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: in Roman numerals forty is written XL

explanation.surface: A question about how a woman named Silvia would get on in Rome once she reaches forty.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's song 'Who is Silvia?' (Two Gentlemen of Verona) says 'She excels each mortal thing'. 'say' signals that XL, spoken as 'ex-ell', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The song praises Silvia as surpassing every other mortal, which is to outdo or shine above them.

clue.text: It must be the 24

definitions.meaning: something that must be is required or indispensable
24 across is 'the ready', slang for money

explanation.surface: A bare statement that something has to be the answer to 24.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 across gives 'the ready', British slang for cash; 'the necessary' is another slang name for money.
explanation.definitionFit: What must be is essential; and 'the necessary' is a slang phrase for funds, like 'the ready'.

clue.text: Drivers causing a riot amid applause

indicators.note: amid says the riot sits in the middle of the applause

parts.note: cheers are shouts of applause
taken as written

explanation.surface: Racing drivers whipping up a riot among a cheering crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' puts ARIOT inside CHEERS. The drivers are those of chariots, as in Roman races.
explanation.definitionFit: Chariot racers were the drivers of horse-drawn chariots.

clue.text: But it's a good lie, whatever the season

definitions.text: But it's a good lie, whatever the season

parts.words: But it's a good lie, whatever the season
parts.note: a bed base with coiled metal inside gives a comfortable place to lie, and its name includes a season of the year, yet it serves in all four

explanation.surface: Someone defending a fib as acceptable at any time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie' is not a falsehood but lying down, and 'season' points to spring, which is in the name though the item is used all year.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprung mattress supports a sleeper comfortably, and its first word names a season.

clue.text: Incisive worker in World War I?

parts.note: the First World War was fought from trenches
a worker is a worker ant

explanation.surface: Someone sharp-witted working through the First World War.
explanation.walkthrough: The ant is in a trench because the Western Front of World War I was fought from trenches; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting, sharp and forceful comment is described this way.

clue.text: The joiner who made Queen Mab's chariot

definitions.text: The joiner who made Queen Mab's chariot

parts.words: The joiner who made Queen Mab's chariot
parts.note: in Romeo and Juliet Mercutio says the fairy queen's carriage is an empty hazelnut made by a nut-gathering animal, the fairies' coachmaker

explanation.surface: A carpenter who built a chariot for a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In Romeo and Juliet Mercutio says Queen Mab's chariot is 'an empty hazel-nut, made by the joiner' of that name, the fairies' coachmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare casts the nut-loving rodent as the fairy carpenter who hollowed out Mab's hazelnut coach.

clue.text: As a sequence even I'd arrange to turn this

indicators.note: the solver is told to arrange the preceding words into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving the letters I and D

explanation.surface: Someone planning the order in which to present things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrange' calls for an anagram of SEQUENCE, EVEN and ID; 'As a' is only a link. An accomplice who turns this testifies against fellow criminals for the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: In British law an accomplice who turns informer testifies for the prosecution under the sovereign's name.

clue.text: Once a miner's piece of land, I do declare !

definitions.note: a cry of surprise, the kind of thing one cries out

parts.note: ex means former, once
a prospector stakes a claim to a plot to mine

explanation.surface: Someone expressing surprise over land a former miner once owned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I do declare!' is an old exclamation of surprise, defining the act of crying out.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out suddenly, as in a surprised outburst.

clue.text: Get one's opponent's at breaking-point in the game, say

indicators.note: say signals a word that sounds like the name of the game

parts.note: conkers is a British children's game with horse chestnuts on strings

explanation.surface: A competitor pushing an opponent to the brink in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In conkers, a British playground game, players swing horse chestnuts on strings at each other's until one breaks. 'say' signals the sound-alike word; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat an opponent is to beat them down until they give way.

clue.text: " That unhoped That men call age " (Brooke)

definitions.text: " That unhoped That men call age " (Brooke)

parts.words: " That unhoped That men call age " (Brooke)
parts.note: the missing word from Rupert Brooke's sonnet 'Safety', where it is used as a noun for a calm untroubled state

explanation.definitionFit: Brooke uses the adjective for calm and untroubled as a noun for the tranquil state of old age.

clue.text: Could the parson, for instance, be lying?

definitions.meaning: a parish priest holding a church living is the holder of that office
an old sense of the word is resting or leaning on something, from Latin for lying down

explanation.surface: A question whether the vicar might be telling untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' means reclining, not telling falsehoods: the word comes from Latin incumbere, to lie on.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman holding a benefice is its holder in office; in its older sense the word means resting upon something.

clue.text: What Roy early to rise can become

definitions.text: What Roy early to rise can become

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, marks the early hours

explanation.surface: An early riser named Roy who might climb to civic office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' reverses ROY plus AM, morning, to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambitious, early-rising local man might become head of the town council.

clue.text: Leave this reel for the fish

indicators.note: the word 'this' plus reel stands for the fish, so taking reel away from the fish leaves the word wanted

parts.note: a conger eel is a large sea fish

explanation.surface: An angler told to leave a fishing reel behind for a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'this reel' as 'this word + REEL': together they make CONGER EEL, so removing REEL leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A congé is permission to depart, or a dismissal, from French for leave.

clue.text: The cash in hand ?

definitions.meaning: British slang for money available to spend
something in hand is prepared and available

explanation.surface: Asking whether the money is in your hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for ready money, cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for available money, and an adjective meaning prepared or at hand.

clue.text: Too early, like the minority

definitions.meaning: minority is the state of being under age, before one is grown up

explanation.surface: Something that happens too soon, as the smaller group would have it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minority' here means being a minor, not the smaller group: read as 'pre-mature', the word describes someone not yet adult.
explanation.definitionFit: Untimely things come before their time; read as two parts, it describes someone not yet grown up.

clue.text: Make regular, journeys in the Strand ?

definitions.meaning: boats and buses that work a route back and forth do this
a strand or layer of rope or yarn

explanation.surface: Commuting regularly along the Strand, the London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a London street, but the capital is a disguise: a strand is a single twist of rope or wool.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel a route regularly, and one of the twisted threads in yarn or rope.

clue.text: The fish to, beat its victim

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
a predator's victim is its prey

explanation.surface: A fish set on thrashing whatever it attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The lamprey is a parasitic fish that latches onto other fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel-like jawless fish that clamps its sucker mouth onto hosts.

clue.text: The present radio release ?

parts.note: a radio is a wireless set
a present is given free of charge

explanation.surface: A radio being given as a gift and launched to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The present radio' reads as a radio set given free; 'release' is the definition, a verb, not a product launch.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a captive is to liberate them.
